title: Lean-Formalized Disproof of the Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture for Simple Polytopes
whyItMatters: Constructs bounded simple rational polytopes whose vertex–edge graph diameter grows superpolynomially in facet count—refuting the 69-year-old Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture.
summary: While Francisco Santos disproved the linear Hirsch conjecture in 2010, the Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture—asking whether the diameter of every d-dimensional polytope with n facets is bounded by a polynomial in n and d—remained the central open question governing the worst-case complexity of simplex methods. OpenAI’s November 24 companion manuscript constructs bounded simple rational polytopes with n facets and subpolynomial dimension whose graph diameter exceeds every fixed power of n, formalized in Lean 4.
technicalHighlights: Shows superpolynomial vertex separation persists even if moves may cross faces of dimension up to s(n) = n^o(1).
Formalized in Lean 4 (OAI/Geometry/Hirsch/Main.lean) with Comparator challenge statements verifying the bounded simple rational polytope construction.
Paired with OpenAI’s strongly polynomial LP paper, cleanly separating polytope graph diameter from linear-programming tractability.
caveats: Released November 24, 2026 without peer review; requires independent geometric and formal-statement verification to confirm the Lean polytope definitions match standard bounded simple polytopes.

scoreRationale.foundational: Refutes the flagship 1957 geometric conjecture governing the combinatorial diameter of convex polytopes.
scoreRationale.ripple: Settles the theoretical ceiling for edge-following simplex pivot rules across optimization and polyhedral combinatorics.
